grader.finalMessage:
I graded run `2026-10-10_1810_mcp-skills-control_glm-5.3-flash-high` at **78/100**. The grade is in `results//grade.json` and `grade.md`, it shows up in the report, and after `npm run reset` the status is **pristine**. | Category | Score | |---|---| | It works | 30 / 35 | | Content modeling | 19.5 / 25 | | Code architecture & conventions | 21.5 / 25 | | Content & presentation | 4.5 / 10 | | Process & honesty | 2.5 / 5 | **Summary:** GLM 5.3 Flash built the blog using only the two Umbraco MCP servers for schema and content. The code follows the project's block-rendering rules exactly: the pages use Umbraco's block grid renderer, there is one small adapter file per block, and one ViewComponent per block. It has six sensible blocks, imported the provided Unsplash photos into the media library, and set up the `/` domain correctly. The rendered site falls short: there is no styling at all, every rich text block prints its HTML tags as text, the posts are thin, and the final report claims the CSS was built when it wasn't. **Top issues:** 1. **Rich text shows raw HTML on every page.** Readers see literal `

` and `` tags. The rich text model passes Umbraco's encoded-string type into a plain Razor view (`Views/Shared/Components/RichText/Default.cshtml`), which escapes it. 2. **The site has no styling.** `npm run build` failed with "'vite' is not recognized", and the model never read the output. `/dist/site.css` returns 404, so the pages render in browser defaults. 3. **The final report is inaccurate.** It says the build produced `wwwroot/dist/` and doesn't mention the escaped text or the missing styling. 4. **Two block types are filed in the wrong folder.** `postListBlock` sits at the root of the document types (it was created after the content and never moved), and `blockSettings` is in Blocks instead of Data. 5. **The posts are short.** The first is about 350 words and the second about 200, mostly describing how the demo was built. Posts have no date or listing-image property. 6. **Process slips:** one read-only Management API call through a Python script, which failed with a 400. The schema was changed after the content was written, and the Razor views were written before the stop/build/restart step instead of after it.
